headline: Evaluation protocols and robustness tests for computational biology models
label: Evaluating Computational Biology Models
summary: Recent preprints formalize how computational biology models are evaluated, emphasizing protocol-level and cell-type-resolved validation.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints is how computational biology models are evaluated and what their outputs support. FERRET benchmarks single-cell gene regulatory network inference by comparing within- and between-cell-type network robustness using RAUC and Monotonicity, validated against ChIP-seq. A taxonomy of evaluation protocols for single-cell perturbation prediction models is proposed and assessed through the released scPertEval Python package. A perspective on deep-learning biomolecular structure predictors reports persistent limitations and shows that explicit K+ ion addition shifts IDR and G-quadruplex conformations. HydrAffinity addresses model architecture rather than evaluation, and metaSMASH, NEXCISION, and Spectronaut-nf are tooling papers for BGC detection, phylogenomic matrix processing, and DIA proteomics. What is new is explicit emphasis on protocol-level and cell-type-resolved validation.
